newsitem.title: INDIA: China may recognise Indian rule in Sikkim-minister.
newsitem.headline: China may recognise Indian rule in Sikkim-minister.

text.p: China is moving towards recognising Indian rule over the disputed Himalayan region of Sikkim, which New Delhi took over in 1975, Foreign Minister Inder Kumar Gujral was quoted as saying on Monday.
The Press Trust of India (PTI) said Gujral told parliament he discussed Sikkim with Chinese President Jiang Zemin during his visit to India last month.
"I did take up Sikkim and there is a move in China towards accepting our view," PTI quoted Gujral as saying.

PTI said opposition leader Atal Bihari Vajpayee of the Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party, speaking in the lower house of parliament, asked Gujral if Sikkim and Arunachal Pradesh state, also in the Himalayas, were discussed with Jiang.
"There is a move in China towards accepting our view and we are hoping of some worthwhile result when officials meet later," the news agency quoted Gujral as saying. It did not elaborate.

Jiang's visit to New Delhi was marked by an agreement to reduce troops and armaments along the Himalayan border. The pact fleshed out an agreement in principle signed by former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao in Beijing in 1993.
Gujral was quoted as saying that when India and China discussed border issues, "we imply this (Sikkim) is ours, once (the) border is agreed and defined".

China claims large parts of Arunachal Pradesh and Sikkim, both states in northeastern India. Chinese officials have in the past said Beijing was ready to concede the annexation of Sikkim to India, but no agreement has been reached.
The border dispute led to a brief war between the two countries in 1962. Relations thawed in 1988 when then Indian prime minister Rajiv Gandhi visited Beijing.
Sikkim is strategically vital to India as it borders Tibet. It was annexed by India in 1975 after its legislature voted to abolish the monarchy and join the Indian union.
Sikkim is hedged by Nepal in the west, Tibet in the north and east, Bhutan in the southeast and India's eastern state of West Bengal in the south.
It had officially been a British protectorate from 1886 until 1947 when India became independent. Three years later it became an Indian protectorate until annexation.
China claims some 90,00 sq km (35,000 sq miles) of Arunachal Pradesh state.
India says Beijing occupies about 33,000 sq km (13,000 sq miles) of the Aksai Chin region which it says is part of Delhi's Jammu and Kashmir state.
